The Haar normalization checks: the two-copy Haar moment on each qutrit is (I+swap)/12; in the purity swap trace the terms with zero or two input swaps each contribute 27, and the two remaining contractions are the realignment and partial-transpose fourth moments. Thus the linear entropy is 5/8−(I_R+I_T)/144. In the real Cartesian spin-one basis, with swap S, Q=3P0=|Ω⟩⟨Ω| for Ω=Σ_i|ii⟩, and x=e^{iα}, y=e^{iβ}, the gate is (1+y)I/2+(1−y)S/2+(x−1)Q/3. Realignment interchanges I,Q and partial transpose interchanges S,Q; both moments can therefore be evaluated on the singlet, antisymmetric and traceless symmetric spaces of dimensions 1,3,5. Independent replay (python /workspace/branches/independent_reproduction.py 5, SymPy) reproduces the entire Laurent phase identity, the elimination factorization, all eight stationary values and Hessian determinants, without executing the supplied code. For exhaustion, B(α)=20+5e^{iα}+2e^{2iα} has modulus at least 13, so β-stationarity lies on two smooth sign branches locally. Along each branch E=A(c)±√Q(c)/216, c=cos α; by β-stationarity the derivative along the branch equals the α partial. For sin α≠0, a necessary equation is 9(Q′)^2−4(65+40c)^2Q=0, whose exact factorization −500(4c+5)(8c+19)(64c²+64c+115) is strictly negative for |c|≤1. At α=0 and π, B is positive real, so the β-stationarity condition gives exactly 0, π/2, π, 3π/2, each also α-stationary. The determinant signs, with positive αα at (0,0) and negative αα at (π,π/2), classify the two definite pairs and two saddle pairs; periodicity and compactness give all global equality cases. This proves the all-phase result analytically, not by sampling. It is specifically for independent Haar pure inputs, unnormalized linear entropy, and spin-invariant two-site unitaries.

value.rationale: The sharp phase-torus benchmark is needed to decide which fully spin-invariant two-qutrit gates maximize Haar-averaged output entanglement, and those gates are directly accessible by tuning two BLBQ couplings. The best invariant gate is not among the four previously analyzed corners (131/324 exceeds 20/81), and even on the α=0 branch the noncorner stationary gates are saddles. Exhaustion and exact stability types show which phase configurations are genuinely optimal rather than extremal only along a chosen evolution; this is a substantive exact classification for a natural family, not a repackaging of the known phase polynomial.
